Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the quick kickoff yesterday. We sketched the high level in the call but wanted to confirm our priorities so the CS->Implementation handoff is clean: SSO via SAML (Okta), SCIM provisioning for groups, IP allowlist for our management CIDR, and a small set of service accounts for batch ingest.

Top asks from our side:
- A recommended mapping between our Okta groups and Redwood roles (we currently have devops, platform-eng, audit-read).
- SCIM attribute mapping for email, displayName, and externalId.
- A safe default for service account TTL/rotation frequency and minimum permissions.
- Timeline: we want prod cutover by May 14 (commercial deadline).

I attached our internal IP ranges and a PDF export of our Okta group structure. Can someone from your team share the mutual action plan (MAP) and a runbook for the cutover windows?

Best,

Quick answers up front:
- We’ll propose a 1:1 mapping for your three Okta groups to Redwood roles: devops -> admin, platform-eng -> deploy, audit-read -> viewer. We’ll include MFA requirements for admin role.
- SCIM attributes: we will request externalId, primaryEmail (userName), displayName; we’ll also flag `roles` as a custom attribute for group sync.
- Service accounts: default TTL 90 days with a recommended rotation automation using our ephemeral-key flow; we’ll propose least-privilege IAM roles scoped to tokenized model access only.
- Timeline: MAP draft by EOD Wed 4/21, runbook draft Thu 4/22, dry-run in staging Fri 5/7, prod cutover target Fri 5/14.

Adding implementation details from the eng side — this will be the basis for the runbook. Please review and call out anything you want changed:

Staging plan (recommended):
- Sandbox Okta -> Redwood staging tenant via SAML (IdP-initiated and SP-initiated tested).
- SCIM: enable group sync only at staging; do not turn on user-provisioning until after role-mapping validation.
- IP allowlist: we will add your staging CIDR first; prod CIDR only added after a successful dry-run.
- Service accounts: create two scoped service accounts for batch-ingest and monitoring. Permissions: read/model-invoke for ingest account; read/metrics for monitoring. Token TTL 90d, rotation via our key-rotation script (link in runbook).

Rollback plan (short):
- If SAML assertion errors exceed 5% of sign-ins in the first 30 minutes, rollback SSO to Okta SSO-only (disable new production SP metadata) and open incident with both teams.
- If SCIM group mapping causes role escalation, revert SCIM sync and run manual role reconciliation.

Docs & artifacts I’ll attach: staging SAML metadata, SCIM attribute mapping JSON, IP checklist, and the rotation script.

Monica
Implementation Lead, Customer Onboarding | Redwood Inference

Attachments: staging-saml-metadata.xml (xml), scim-attribute-map.json (json), service-account-rotation.sh (sh)

Operational notes from SRE perspective — a few constraints and a recommended checklist to include in the runbook:

Constraints:
- IP allowlist changes to prod require a signed maintenance window and will deploy through our infra change pipeline (30–45 min lead time).
- Service account keys created via console are audited in our logs; we will require the `externalId` tag on keys to map to XenoBank ticket ids.

Runbook checklist (to be included as section 2):
1) Pre-cutover verification (owner: XenoBank): test Okta sandbox SAML login with 3 users from each mapped group.
2) Redwood staging verification (owner: Redwood): validate SCIM group sync and confirm role bindings in staging dashboard.
3) Dry-run (joint): create service accounts, exercise TTL rotation, and ping from XenoBank staging IPs.
4) Maintenance window (joint): add prod CIDR, flip SCIM to prod (if applicable), validate sign-ins + provisioning, monitor logs for 1 hour.
5) Rollback steps and postmortem triggers.

I’ll add the infra change runbook link and a short checklist for audit evidence capture (SOC2: user provisioning logs, IP-modification audit).

— Priyom
SRE | Redwood Inference

Attachments: infra-change-playbook.md (md)
